title: Factbox-Tech leaders, Wall Street CEOs, governments split over 'AI doom' fears
key_facts: Amodei's essay 'We Must Pace the Frontier' says AI progress has accelerated drastically faster since summer 2026
Altman and Musk backed Amodei; OpenAI will adopt independent evaluators and publish reports on unexpected AI behaviour
Zuckerberg rejected a slowdown, per the Financial Times, saying each lab is responsible for its own safety
Huang told CBS there is a '0% chance' AI is the end of the world and agreed no new regulations are needed
Fink told CNBC a data-centre moratorium would mean recession
Banks financing the AI buildout could face credit losses if it slows
quote_evidence: AI industry leaders are split over how fast companies should develop the increasingly powerful technology, as Anthropic's Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman and SpaceX's Elon Musk call for a coordinated slowdown.
"2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world," Huang told CBS News.
why_it_matters_hint: A single page of who sits where in the pace-of-AI argument.
notes: Read the Reuters factbox as carried by the Lufkin Daily News (copy site); source credited to Reuters. Url is the copy page, as the original Reuters link was not available. Score lowered 6 to 5: compiles earlier statements.
